problems.title: Detaching the ODE state breaks the gradients used for airfoil editing
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, arXiv v4 PDF pp. 5–6; Appendix B, Algorithm 3, p. 17; sample_process_with_log_prob composite_drift.
claim: Section 3.2, PDF pp. 5–6, and Appendix B, Algorithm 3, PDF p. 17, differentiate editing loss through the sampled ODE trajectory. Released airfoil_generation/model/optimal_transport_functional_flow_model.py, OptimalTransportFunctionalFlowForRegression.sample_process_with_log_prob, lines 1202–1371, detaches the state inside composite_drift at lines 1271–1278, while using ordinary Euler differentiation.
analysis: Take \(u_0=1\), \(v_a(u)=au\), \(a=0.4\), and two Euler steps of size \(1/2\). The forward endpoint is \((1+0.5a)^2u_0=1.44\), with derivatives \(\partial u_1/\partial u_0=1.44\) and \(\partial u_1/\partial a=1.2\). Detaching drift inputs preserves the forward value but keeps only the direct state path and local parameter terms, giving derivatives \(1\) and \(0.5+0.6=1.1\). Matching forward output therefore does not validate those editing gradients.
result: Current editing code omits state-chain-rule terms, with explicit scalar derivative discrepancies; forward generation and benchmark editing errors have not been refuted.
repair: Preserve the incoming ODE state graph, enabling local state differentiation only when necessary without replacing the state by a detached leaf. This restores the ordinary Euler sensitivity recurrence; density and solver alternatives still need separate checks.
problems.impact_rationale: Current editing code omits state-chain-rule terms, with explicit scalar derivative discrepancies; forward generation and benchmark editing errors have not been refuted.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Jointly changing the density is not equivalent to MAP under a fixed pretrained prior
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Eq. (7), PDF p. 5; joint optimization discussion, PDF p. 6.
claim: Section 3.2, Eq. (7), PDF p. 5, derives an edited-sample posterior under a trained prior and drops evidence constant in the sample. The subsequent procedure on PDF p. 6 and Algorithm 3 optimizes both the sample-generating flow and its initial function, so the density itself changes.
analysis: A fixed-prior MAP objective is reconstruction cost minus \(\log p_{\theta_0}(u')\). Changing \(\theta\) while evaluating \(p_\theta(u')\) changes the reference density. For the smooth scalar contracting flow \(F_c(a)=e^{-c}a\) with standard-normal base and fixed sample \(a=u'=0\), reconstruction stays zero but negative log density is \(\tfrac12\log(2\pi)-c\), decreasing without bound as \(c\to\infty\). A fixed pretrained density assigns that unchanged sample a fixed cost. This proves non-equivalence, not collapse of the actual airfoil model.
result: A smooth invertible contraction changes self-density at a fixed edited sample, disproving fixed-prior MAP equivalence without demonstrating actual model collapse.
repair: An intended adaptive-density editing heuristic is consistent with the implemented scalar objective. Under that interpretation, the objective is not inherently a programming error; the needed correction is to state its changing reference distribution and avoid presenting the fixed-prior Bayes calculation as an equivalence proof. If the intended posterior is instead \(p_\theta(u'\mid z)\) while also optimizing \(\theta\), its evidence \(p_\theta(z)\) generally depends on \(\theta\) and cannot be dropped merely because it is constant in \(u'\). If a joint posterior over \(u'\) and \(\theta\) is intended, it requires an explicit model/prior for \(\theta\); Eq. (7) does not provide one. These are distinct modeling choices.
problems.impact_rationale: A smooth invertible contraction changes self-density at a fixed edited sample, disproving fixed-prior MAP equivalence without demonstrating actual model collapse.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Raw smoothness and diversity scores change under resampling of the same airfoils
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, Eq. (9), PDF p. 6; Section 4.2, Table 2, PDF pp. 7–8.
claim: Paraphrase: Section 4.1, p. 6, defines the smoothness score in Eq. (9) as the sum of distances from each point to the line through its two neighbors. It defines diversity through log determinants of similarity matrices based on Euclidean distances between sampled airfoils. Section 4.2 and Table 2, pp. 7–8, compare generated airfoils at \(257\), \(513\), and \(1025\) points using those metrics to assess resolution changes. The question here is whether raw score changes can be attributed to geometric quality or diversity independently of sampling resolution.

The released super-resolution evaluator implements at lines 249–270 and at \(273\)–285. Smoothness is an unnormalized sum. Diversity flattens all coordinates, computes Euclidean pair distances \(d\), forms \(S_{ij}=\exp(-d_{ij}^2/2)\), and reports a log determinant. There is no quadrature or point-count normalization.
analysis: For a fixed radius-\(R\) circle sampled at \(N\) equally spaced points, the raw neighbor-chord distance sum is \(NR(1-\cos(2\pi/N))\sim2\pi^2R/N\), although geometry is unchanged. For two fixed sinusoidal airfoils with amplitudes \(b_1,b_2\), unweighted squared separation is \((b_2-b_1)^2(N-1)/2\), so their kernel log determinant also changes with \(N\) while continuous squared separation remains \((b_2-b_1)^2/2\). Cross-resolution interpretation requires an explicit sampling normalization.
result: Supported metric-scope qualification; within-resolution comparisons remain interpretable.
repair: Compare smoothness on a common reference grid, or define a justified continuous regularity functional. Use a fixed-bandwidth quadrature distance for diversity so point-count changes do not change the underlying geometry measure.
problems.impact_rationale: The same continuous shapes have resolution-dependent raw metrics, limiting cross-resolution interpretation while leaving comparisons on a common grid intact.

impact_rationale: Latest paper and current editing code retain local derivative and probabilistic-interpretation gaps plus resolution-dependent metrics. No trained airfoil model, CFD result or same-resolution performance comparison is invalidated.
